readings.title: The Promise of Isaac Renewed
readings.text: [Genesis 18:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to him by the terebinth trees of Mamre, while he was sitting in the tent door in the heat of the day. [2] And he lifted his eyes and looked, and saw three men standing opposite him. And when he saw them, he ran from the tent door to meet them, and bowed himself to the ground, [3] and said, “<dn>Master</dn>, if I have now found favour in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, please do not pass <dn>your</dn> servant by. [4] “Please let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree. [5] “And let me bring a piece of bread, and refresh your hearts, and then go on, for this is why you have come to your servant.” And they said, “Do as you have said.” [6] And Abraham ran into the tent to Sarah and said, “Hurry, make ready three measures of fine meal, knead it and make cakes.” [7] And Abraham ran to the herd, took a tender and good calf, and gave it to a young man, and he hurried to prepare it. [8] And he took curds and milk and the calf which he had prepared, and set it before them. And he stood by them under the tree as they ate. [9] And they said to him, “Where is Sarah your wife?” And he said, “See, in the tent.” [10] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall certainly return to you according to the time of life, and see, Sarah your wife is to have a son!”</dq> And Sarah was listening in the tent door which was behind him. [11] Now Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age, and Sarah had passed the way of women. [12] And Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old, shall I have pleasure, my master being old too?” [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Abraham, <dq>“Why did Sarah laugh, saying, ‘Shall I truly have a child, since I am old?’</dq> [14] <dq>“Is any matter too hard for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? At the appointed time <dn>I</dn> return to you, according to the time of life, and Sarah has a son.”</dq> [15] But Sarah denied it, saying, “I did not laugh,” for she was afraid. And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“No, but you did laugh!”</dq>

readings.title: Abraham Intercedes for Sodom
readings.text: [Genesis 18:16] And the men rose up from there and looked toward Seḏom, and Abraham went with them to send them away. [17] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Shall <dn>I</dn> hide from Abraham what <dn>I</dn> am doing,</dq> [18] <dq>since Abraham is certainly going to become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?</dq> [19] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have known him, so that he commands his children and his household after him, to guard the way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to do righteousness and right-ruling, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings to Abraham what <dn>He</dn> has spoken to him.”</dq> [20] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Because the outcry against Seḏom and Amorah is great, and because their sin is very heavy,</dq> [21] <dq><dn>I</dn> am going down now to see whether they have done altogether according to the outcry against it that has come to <dn>Me</dn>, and if not, <dn>I</dn> know.”</dq> [22] And the men turned away from there and went toward Seḏom, but Abraham still stood before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [23] And Abraham drew near and said, “Would <dn>You</dn> also destroy the righteous with the wrong? [24] “Suppose there are fifty righteous within the city, would <dn>You</dn> also destroy the place and not spare it for the fifty righteous that are in it? [25] “Far be it from <dn>You</dn> to act in this way, to put the righteous to death with the wrong, so that the righteous should be as the wrong. Far be it from <dn>You</dn>! Does the Judge of all the earth not do right-ruling?” [26] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“If <dn>I</dn> find in Seḏom fifty righteous within the city, then <dn>I</dn> shall spare all the place for their sakes.”</dq> [27] And Abraham answered and said, “See now, I have taken it upon myself to speak to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, I who am but dust and ashes. [28] “Suppose there are five less than the fifty righteous, would <dn>You</dn> destroy all of the city for lack of five?” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“If <dn>I</dn> find there forty-five, <dn>I</dn> do not destroy it.”</dq> [29] And he spoke to <dn>Him</dn> yet again and said, “Suppose there are found forty there?” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> do not do it for the sake of forty.”</dq> [30] And he said, “Let not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be displeased, and let me speak: Suppose there are found thirty there?” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> do not do it if <dn>I</dn> find thirty there.”</dq> [31] And he said, “See now, I have taken it upon myself to speak to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: Suppose there are found twenty there?” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> do not destroy it for the sake of twenty.”</dq> [32] And he said, “Let not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be displeased, and let me speak only this time: Suppose there are found ten there?” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> do not destroy it for the sake of ten.”</dq> [33] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went <dn>His</dn> way as soon as <dn>He</dn> had ended speaking to Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.

readings.title: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
readings.text: [Genesis 19:1] And the two messengers came to Seḏom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gate of Seḏom. And Lot saw them, and rose up to meet them, and he bowed himself with his face toward the ground. [2] And he said, “Look, please, my masters, please turn in to your servant’s house and spend the night, and wash your feet, and rise early and go on your way.” And they said, “No, but let us spend the night in the open square.” [3] But he urged them strongly, and they turned in to him and entered his house. And he made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread, and they ate. [4] Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Seḏom, both old and young, all the people from every part, surrounded the house. [5] And they called to Lot and said to him, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, and let us know them.” [6] And Lot went out to them through the doorway, and shut the door behind him, [7] and said, “Please, my brothers, do not do evil! [8] “Look, please, I have two daughters who have not known a man. Please, let me bring them out to you, and do to them as is good in your eyes. Only do nothing to these men, because they have come under the shadow of my roof.” [9] But they said, “Stand back!” And they said, “This one came in to sojourn, and should he always judge? Now we are going to treat you worse than them.” So they pressed hard against the man Lot, and came near to break down the door. [10] And the men reached out their hands and pulled Lot into the house with them, and shut the door. [11] And they struck the men who were at the doorway of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they weary themselves to find the door. [12] And the men said to Lot, “Have you anyone else here? Son-in-law, and your sons, and your daughters, and whomever you have in the city – bring them out of this place! [13] “For we are going to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has grown great before the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent us to destroy it.” [14] And Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who had married his daughters, and said, “Get up, get out of this place, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is going to destroy this city!” But to his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking. [15] And when the morning dawned, the messengers urged Lot to hurry, saying, “Arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are here, lest you be consumed in the punishment of the city.” [16] And while he lingered, the men took hold of his hand, and the hand of his wife, and the hands of his two daughters, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> having compassion on him, and they brought him out and set him outside the city. [17] And it came to be, when they had brought them outside, that he said, “Escape for your life! Do not look behind you nor stay anywhere in the plain. Escape to the mountains, lest you be consumed.” [18] And Lot said to them, “Oh no, <dn>Master</dn>! [19] “See now, <dn>your</dn> servant has found favour in <dn>your</dn> eyes, and <dn>you</dn> have increased <dn>your</dn> kindness which <dn>you</dn> have shown me by saving my life, but I am unable to escape to the mountains, lest calamity overtake me and I die. [20] “See now, this city is near enough to flee to, and it is small. Please let me escape there – is it not a small matter? – and let my life be saved.” [21] And <dn>he</dn> said to him, <dq>“Look, <dn>I</dn> have favoured you concerning this matter also, without overthrowing this city for which you have spoken.</dq> [22] <dq>“Hurry, escape there. For <dn>I</dn> am unable to do any deed until you come there.”</dq> Therefore the name of the city was called Tso‛ar. [23] The sun had risen upon the earth when Lot entered Tso‛ar. [24] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rained sulphur and fire on Seḏom and Amorah, from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> out of the heavens. [25] So <dn>He</dn> overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and what grew on the ground. [26] But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a column of salt. [27] And Abraham arose early in the morning and went to the place where he had stood before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [28] And he looked toward Seḏom and Amorah, and toward all the land of the plain. And he looked and saw the smoke of the land which went up like the smoke of a furnace. [29] And it came to be, when <dn>Elohim</dn> destroyed the cities of the plain, that <dn>Elohim</dn> remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when <dn>He</dn> overthrew the cities in which Lot had dwelt.

readings.title: The Origin of Moab and Ammon
readings.text: [Genesis 19:30] And Lot went up out of Tso‛ar and dwelt in the mountains, and his two daughters with him, for he was afraid to dwell in Tso‛ar. And he and his two daughters dwelt in a cave. [31] And the first-born said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no man on the earth to come in to us as is the way of all the earth. [32] “Come, let us make our father drink wine, and lie with him, so that we preserve the seed of our father.” [33] So they made their father drink wine that night. And the first-born went in and lay with her father, and he was not aware of her lying down or her rising up. [34] And it came to be on the next day that the first-born said to the younger, “See, I lay with my father last night. Let us make him drink wine tonight as well, and you go in and lie with him, so that we preserve the seed of our father.” [35] So they made their father drink wine that night as well. And the younger arose and lay with him, and he was not aware of her lying down or her rising up. [36] Thus both the daughters of Lot were with child by their father. [37] And the first-born bore a son and called his name Mo’aḇ. He is the father of the Mo’aḇites to this day. [38] And the younger, she also bore a son and called his name Ben-Ammi. He is the father of the children of Ammon to this day.

readings.title: Abraham and Abimelek
readings.text: [Genesis 20:1] And Abraham journeyed from there to the land of the South, and dwelt between Qaḏesh and Shur, and stayed in Gerar. [2] And Abraham said concerning Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” And Aḇimeleḵ sovereign of Gerar sent and took Sarah. [3] But <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Aḇimeleḵ in a dream by night, and said to him, <dq>“See, you are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken, for she is a man’s wife.”</dq> [4] However, Aḇimeleḵ had not come near her, and he said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, would <dn>You</dn> slay a righteous nation also? [5] “Did he not say to me, ‘She is my sister’? And she, even she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ In the integrity of my heart and innocence of my hands I have done this.” [6] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him in a dream, <dq>“Yea, <dn>I</dn> know that you did this in the integrity of your heart, and so <dn>I</dn> kept you from sinning against <dn>Me</dn>. For this reason <dn>I</dn> did not let you touch her.</dq> [7] <dq>“And now, return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and let him pray for you and you live. But if you do not return her, know that you shall certainly die, you and all that are yours.”</dq> [8] And Aḇimeleḵ rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and spoke all these words in their hearing. And the men were very much afraid. [9] And Aḇimeleḵ called Abraham and said to him, “What have you done to us? In what have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that should not be done.” [10] And Aḇimeleḵ said to Abraham, “What did you have in view, that you have done this matter?” [11] And Abraham said, “Only because I said to myself, ‘The fear of <dn>Elohim</dn> is not in this place, and they shall kill me for the sake of my wife.’ [12] “And yet, she is truly my sister. She is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife. [13] “And it came to be, when <dn>Elohim</dn> caused me to wander from my father’s house, that I said to her, ‘This is your kindness that you show me: in every place where we go, say of me, “He is my brother.” ’ ” [14] And Aḇimeleḵ took sheep, and oxen, and male and female servants, and gave them to Abraham. And he restored Sarah his wife to him. [15] And Aḇimeleḵ said, “See, my land is before you, dwell wherever it is good in your eyes.” [16] And to Sarah he said, “See, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. See, it is to you a covering of eyes before all who are with you and before all others, and you are cleared.” [17] And Abraham prayed to <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>Elohim</dn> healed Aḇimeleḵ, and his wife, and his female servants, and they bore children. [18] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had closed up every womb of the house of Aḇimeleḵ because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

readings.title: The Birth of Isaac
readings.text: [Genesis 21:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> visited Sarah as <dn>He</dn> had said, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did to Sarah as <dn>He</dn> had spoken. [2] So Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time of which <dn>Elohim</dn> had spoken to him. [3] And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Yitsḥaq. [4] And Abraham circumcised his son Yitsḥaq when he was eight days old, as <dn>Elohim</dn> had commanded him. [5] And Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Yitsḥaq was born to him. [6] And Sarah said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of it laughs with me.” [7] And she said, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah should nurse children? For I have borne him a son in his old age.”
